verdict.rationale: Linear's agent docs show that an agent is built as an OAuth app requesting specific scopes, such as `app:assignable` and `app:mentionable`. The API supports OAuth2 alongside personal API keys, and admins can approve third-party apps before install. That points to scoped credentials for agents, but the evidence lists only these agent-specific scopes and never documents a general read/write or per-team permission model, or whether personal API keys can be restricted. missing for 10: documented full scope catalog (read/write/resource-level), scoped or restricted personal API keys, per-team or per-resource credential restriction, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: app:assignable | Allow the app to be assigned as a delegate on issues and made a member of projects app:mentionable | Allow the app to be mentioned in issues, documents, and other editor surfaces
The Linear API supports personal API keys and OAuth2 authentication.
Third-party app approvals are now available on paid Linear plans, allowing admins to review and approve apps before they're installed.
